name: Bone Grafting
shortDescription: Rebuilds lost jawbone so implants have a stable foundation.

seo.title: Bone Grafting in Santa Clarita | Dr. Neda Moezzi
seo.description: Bone grafting in Santa Clarita with Dr. Neda Moezzi: socket preservation, ridge augmentation, sinus lifts and PRF-based holistic options before implants.

hero.lead: When the jaw has lost bone after an extraction, infection or years of missing teeth, a graft rebuilds it. Dr. Neda Moezzi plans each graft with 3D imaging and offers PRF-based holistic options.
hero.imageAlt: Dr. Neda Moezzi treating a patient in the office

intro.heading: Rebuilding the foundation for your smile
paragraphs: Bone grafting sounds more dramatic than it is. In practice it is a planned, well-tolerated procedure that adds bone where the jaw has thinned, usually after a tooth is lost, an infection has done damage or a denture has been worn for years. At Valencia Smile Expert in Santa Clarita, Dr. Moezzi most often uses grafting to prepare a site for a dental implant or to preserve bone right after an extraction.

Without enough healthy bone, an implant has nothing solid to hold onto and the face can begin to lose its natural contour. A graft gives your body a scaffold to rebuild on. Over several weeks to a few months, your own bone grows into and replaces the graft material. Dr. Moezzi uses 3D imaging to plan each graft and offers PRF and other natural options for patients who prefer them.

whoItsFor.heading: Who it's for
whoItsFor.intro: Grafting is usually recommended when the jaw has lost bone or needs building up before implants.
items: You have lost a tooth and want to keep the jawbone from shrinking
You want dental implants but do not have enough bone to support them
You have noticed facial sagging or bone loss from teeth missing for some time
Your bite has become unstable and needs a stronger foundation
You need an upper back implant and the sinus sits too close to the ridge

benefits.heading: Why bone grafting matters
benefits.intro: A graft is an investment in everything that comes after it.

items.title: Makes implants possible
items.text: Rebuilt bone gives an implant the volume and density it needs to integrate and stay stable.

items.title: Preserves the jaw after extraction
items.text: A socket graft placed at the time of removal keeps the ridge from collapsing inward.

items.title: Supports facial contours
items.text: Maintaining jawbone helps prevent the sunken look that follows long-term tooth loss.

items.title: A more stable bite
items.text: A solid ridge supports restorations that distribute chewing forces evenly.

items.title: Natural options available
items.text: PRF and your own bone can be used for patients who prefer to avoid donor or synthetic material.

options.heading: Types of grafts and materials
options.intro: Dr. Moezzi matches the graft type and material to your anatomy, your timeline and your preferences.

items.title: Socket preservation
items.text: Placed right after a tooth is removed to hold the height and width of the ridge for a future implant.

items.title: Ridge augmentation
items.text: Restores the natural contour of the jawbone after trauma or prolonged tooth loss, creating a stable base for implants.

items.title: Sinus lift
items.text: Adds bone to the upper jaw beneath the sinus, commonly needed before placing implants in the back upper teeth.

items.title: Allograft
items.text: Processed donated human bone with no living cells, leaving a mineral matrix with natural growth factors that signal your body to rebuild bone.

items.title: Xenograft
items.text: Bone from an animal source, usually bovine, fully processed to leave a strong, sterile scaffold.

items.title: Synthetic graft
items.text: Lab-made material that mimics natural bone structure, for patients who prefer a non-biological source.

items.title: Holistic options: PRF and your own bone
items.text: PRF made from your blood supports healing, and autologous grafts use bone from elsewhere in your mouth, with no synthetic additives.

process.heading: The bone grafting process
process.intro: Three stages, each explained before it happens.

steps.title: Consultation and imaging
steps.text: A detailed exam and a 3D CBCT scan measure your bone volume and show where it is needed. Dr. Moezzi walks you through the graft options and answers your questions before anything is decided.

steps.title: In-office graft procedure
steps.text: The graft is placed in our Valencia office under local anesthesia, with sedation if planned. The material is positioned at the site, then covered and stabilized so healing can begin.

steps.title: Healing and follow-up
steps.text: Healing takes several weeks to a few months depending on the graft. Follow-up visits track your progress, and Dr. Moezzi tells you when the site is ready for the next step, such as implant placement.

technology.heading: Imaging and biologics
technology.intro: Good grafting starts with seeing the bone clearly and giving it what it needs to regrow.

items.title: 3D CBCT imaging
items.text: Measures bone height, width and density in three dimensions so the graft is planned precisely.

items.title: PRF therapy
items.text: Platelet-rich fibrin spun from a small sample of your blood is mixed with or layered over the graft to support healing.

items.title: Guided implant surgery
items.text: Once the graft matures, the same digital plan guides the implant into the rebuilt bone.

aftercare.heading: Before and after your graft
before: Follow fasting instructions if sedation is planned
Avoid smoking and alcohol for at least 24 hours before your appointment
Pause medications only if Dr. Moezzi advises it
Arrange transportation home if you will be sedated
Keep up good oral hygiene to lower the risk of infection
after: Rest for the first 24 to 48 hours and avoid strenuous activity
Use cold compresses to manage swelling
Take all prescribed medication as directed
Eat soft, cool foods such as yogurt, smoothies and applesauce
Avoid straws, smoking and forceful rinsing
Rinse gently with saltwater to keep the area clean

cost.heading: Cost and financing
cost.text: The cost of a bone graft depends on its type and size, the material used and whether it is combined with an extraction or implant placement. A small socket graft and a sinus lift are very different procedures, so we do not post one price. After your exam and 3D scan, Dr. Moezzi gives you a written estimate that itemizes each step before treatment is scheduled. We accept most major PPO plans and will help you understand what yours covers. Flexible financing is available, and new patients can begin with our $59 exam and X-rays special.

faqs.a: Most patients report only mild discomfort. The graft is placed under local anesthesia, with sedation options if you prefer, so the procedure itself should not hurt. Some soreness and swelling in the days afterward is normal and usually eases with cold compresses and the medication Dr. Moezzi recommends.

faqs.q: How long does it take to heal after a bone graft?
faqs.a: The gums typically close over the site within a few weeks. Full integration, where your own bone has grown through the graft, usually takes three to six months, depending on your health, the size of the graft and the material used. Follow-up visits track your progress along the way.

faqs.q: Can I get a dental implant immediately after bone grafting?
faqs.a: Sometimes. If the graft is small and the surrounding bone is sound, an implant can occasionally be placed at the same visit. More often the graft needs to heal and mature for a few months first so the implant has solid bone to hold onto. Dr. Moezzi sets a timeline based on your scan.

faqs.q: What kind of bone is used for grafting?
faqs.a: Options include your own bone taken from another area of your mouth, processed donor bone, bovine-derived bone and synthetic materials. All are biocompatible and widely used. For patients who prefer a fully natural approach, PRF from your own blood and autologous bone avoid outside materials. Each option is explained at your consultation.

faqs.q: Where can I learn more about dental bone grafting?
faqs.a: The Cleveland Clinic publishes a clear patient overview of dental bone grafts that covers the basics well. For questions about your own jaw, a consultation is more useful. Dr. Moezzi can show you your 3D scan and explain exactly where bone is needed and which graft approach fits. Call (661) 254-5200 to arrange one.

cta.heading: Rebuild the foundation, then the smile
cta.text: Start with an exam and a 3D scan in our Valencia office. You will leave knowing whether grafting is needed, what it involves and what it costs. Patients visit us from across Santa Clarita, Stevenson Ranch, Newhall, Saugus and Canyon Country.
